response:
It sounds like you've genuinely reflected on this and feel pretty settled about it—that's fair, and not everyone reacts to a divorce the same way. Feeling neutral isn't wrong, and you're right that your parents' ongoing conflict is their responsibility to sort out, not yours.

That said, going to counseling doesn't require you to have big emotions to "perform." Even one or two sessions could just be a low-pressure space to talk about how their fighting affects you, or about anything else going on in your life. Trying to dodge it with the homework excuse might create more tension than just being honest. You could tell your parents plainly: "I don't feel much about the divorce, but I'll go a couple times." If it truly feels useless afterward, you'll have a real basis to say so. Sometimes feelings show up later, too, and it can help to already have someone to talk to if they do.
